lessons: Review snagged with green checks and two fixable findings. It accepted the serial slot, re-gate ordering, tree-hash refusal, both rungs and the git seams. Keep all of that; change only _path_matches and the rung-2 abort path in mergequeue.py, plus tests.

Rewrite _path_matches to match the scope-fence prefix rule: path == declared or path.startswith(declared if declared.endswith('/') else declared + '/'). Drop fnmatch and its import; glob characters are literal.

Add tests: a declared prefix with no trailing slash (e.g. 'generated') resolves the nested conflict 'generated/x.lock' through rung 1, and a glob-looking entry (e.g. '*.lock') is not expanded, so the conflict falls to rung 2.

In _rebase, abort in exactly one place. Have the loop return the rung-2 facts, then run a single rebase_abort unwind step. Do not also call abort from inside the loop and again from except BaseException.

If that single rebase_abort raises GitError on the rung-2 path, journal the conflict facts and return a typed gate_failed Admission with CandidateRebaseFinding. A raw GitError must never escape admit. Add a test with an abort that fails (a Git stub).
reason: Review found two concrete, locally fixable correctness defects with explicit paved roads; the rest of the design was accepted and all checks are green.
